events.title: Malta Surrenders to Napoleon
events.description: After the French invasion of Malta, the Knights Hospitaller surrendered the island to Napoleon Bonaparte. That began about two years of French occupation.
events.significance: The surrender ended the centuries-long rule of the Knights over Malta. It also brought the island into the Napoleonic Wars, and Britain later took control of it.

events.title: Philippines Declares Independence
events.description: Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain at Kawit, Cavite. The Philippine flag was raised in public for the first time.
events.significance: The proclamation marked the start of the first Philippine Republic in Asia. June 12 is now celebrated as Independence Day in the Philippines.

events.title: Anne Frank Is Born
events.description: Annelies Marie Frank was born in Frankfurt, Germany. She later went into hiding in Amsterdam during the Nazi occupation and kept a diary there.
events.significance: Her diary became one of the most widely read testimonies of the Holocaust. It remains a powerful symbol of the human cost of persecution.

events.title: Reagan Challenges Gorbachev at the Berlin Wall
events.description: In a speech at the Brandenburg Gate in West Berlin, U.S. President Ronald Reagan called on Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev to tear down the Berlin Wall.
events.significance: The speech became one of the best-known moments of the late Cold War. The Wall fell in 1989.

events.title: The Boeing 777 Takes Flight
events.description: The Boeing 777, the world's largest twin-engine jetliner, made its first flight.
events.significance: The 777 changed long-haul air travel by showing that a twin-engine jet could fly efficiently over long routes. It became a mainstay of airlines worldwide.
